fix.notes: The fix is entirely mechanical — `cached_property` stores the result in the instance dict after first access, so subsequent attribute lookups on the same View object return the string directly without re-entering the descriptor. Each HTTP request creates a fresh View instance, so there is no cross-request state leakage.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The `header.mustache` template references `notice_html` twice — once as a section guard (`{{#notice_html}}`) and once as the rendered value (`{{{notice_html}}}`). Pystache calls the method for each reference, so `notice_html()` ran twice per page request. This method can do a database query (loading the PD500 competition) and renders a template, making the double call both wasteful and noisy in logs.

## What changed

Decorated `View.notice_html` in `decksite/view.py` with `@functools.cached_property`. On the first pystache lookup the method runs and the result is stored in the instance dict; on the second lookup Python's normal attribute resolution returns the cached string directly without invoking the descriptor again.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks passed)
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 845 passed, 1 skipped, 89 deselected

Fixes #12182
